title: The Inheritance of Saint Alder's
premise: When insurance investigator Emrys Almeida is sent to appraise the estate of Saint Alder's, a shuttered coastal sanatorium, he discovers the diary of missing archivist Lena Voss — and entries written in her hand dated weeks after her disappearance. His photographic memory begins matching the diary's details against a thirty-year-old fire that killed four patients, a fire the town has agreed to misremember. As Emrys reconstructs the alibis of the sanatorium's founding families, he realizes the diary's later entries are forgeries designed to frame him, and that the trial now looming over Saint Alder's was engineered to bury the truth one final time. In the end, Emrys testifies from memory alone, toppling the Voss family patriarch — but chooses to leave one name out of the record: his own father's.
about_author: Bram Crane is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating suspicious losses along the New England coast before turning to fiction. He writes in longhand at a desk salvaged from a decommissioned lighthouse keeper's station.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Emrys Almeida arrives at Saint Alder's to assess storm damage on an estate claim, cataloguing the decaying sanatorium with his flawless recall. He finds Lena Voss's diary wedged behind a filing cabinet. POV: Emrys. Beat: quiet unease beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Reading the diary at his motel, Emrys realizes the final entries postdate Lena's disappearance by three weeks — and describe him arriving at the estate. POV: Emrys. Beat: the chill of being written into someone else's story.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Emrys interviews estate executor Marguerite Voss, Lena's aunt, whose alibi for the 1994 fire is polished to a shine. The town's warmth toward her feels rehearsed. POV: Emrys. Beat: suspicion dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: A retired nurse, Ida Brennan, lets slip that four patients died in the fire, not two as recorded. She begs Emrys to forget she said it. POV: Emrys. Beat: the cost of knowing.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Emrys cross-references the fire night using his memory of old claim files: every founding family has an account, and every account corroborates the others too perfectly. POV: Emrys. Beat: the elegance of a lie well kept.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Problem
chapters.summary: Emrys brings the diary to a document examiner friend; the late entries are traced forgeries by someone who knew Lena intimately. POV: alternating Emrys and the examiner, Ruth. Beat: proof arrives, but so does danger.

chapters.title: Someone in the Archive
chapters.summary: Returning to Saint Alder's at night, Emrys finds the diary's hiding place emptied and fresh boot prints in coal dust. He memorizes everything before it can be erased. POV: Emrys. Beat: hunted, not hunter.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Grief
chapters.summary: Marguerite, confronted gently, breaks: Lena had found something in the patient records and called her the week she vanished. POV: Marguerite. Beat: complicity curdling into terror.

chapters.title: The Trial Docket
chapters.summary: News breaks: the county is finally prosecuting the 1994 fire, and Emrys is named a material witness — scheduled, conveniently, after any testimony he might give could be discredited. POV: Emrys. Beat: the trap closing politely.

chapters.title: Ida's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Ida admits she falsified death certificates under orders from Dr. Edwin Voss, Marguerite's father, to hide that the patients were locked in. POV: Ida. Beat: guilt after three decades of silence.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Emrys watches his father, then a hospital orderly, come home the night of the fire smelling of smoke. POV: Emrys (memory). Beat: dread of what memory refuses to release.

chapters.title: Lena's Last Week
chapters.summary: Reconstructing from receipts, phone logs, and the genuine early diary entries, Emrys maps Lena's final days: she met someone at the boathouse the night she disappeared. POV: Emrys. Beat: methodical hope.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Searching the collapsed boathouse, Emrys finds Lena's hidden duplicate records — patient logs proving the fire doors were chained. Someone watches him leave. POV: Emrys. Beat: triumph shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: An Offer, Politely Made
chapters.summary: Dr. Edwin Voss invites Emrys to dinner and offers him a consultancy, a house, a future — if the records stay lost. Emrys declines with perfect courtesy. POV: Emrys. Beat: corruption wearing its best face.

chapters.title: Ruth Burns Bright
chapters.summary: The document examiner's office goes up in flames; Ruth survives but the forged pages' originals are destroyed. Emrys recognizes the accelerant pattern instantly. POV: Ruth. Beat: fear becoming fury.

chapters.title: The Pattern of Fire
chapters.summary: Emrys matches the arson signature to a 1994 insurance claim he once processed — filed by his own father, the orderly turned 'fire investigator.' POV: Emrys. Beat: the floor giving way beneath identity.

chapters.title: Father and Son
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts his father, who confesses he set the 1994 fire on Edwin Voss's orders and helped stage Lena's disappearance to protect them both. POV: alternating father and son. Beat: love and betrayal indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Where Lena Is
chapters.summary: The father reveals Lena is alive — hidden these months by Edwin, who needed her 'missing' until the trial buried the case. Emrys must find her before Edwin decides otherwise. POV: Emrys. Beat: desperate clock.

chapters.title: The Chapel of Saint Alder
chapters.summary: Emrys deduces Lena is held in the sanatorium's sealed chapel ward; he and Marguerite, choosing truth over family, extract her through the old service tunnels. POV: Marguerite. Beat: redemption purchased at price.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: At trial, Emrys recites the patient logs, the chained doors, the forged diary, and the arson pattern from memory alone, dismantling thirty years of woven alibis. Edwin Voss is indicted. POV: Emrys. Beat: the quiet thunder of truth spoken plainly.

chapters.title: The Name Left Out
chapters.summary: Facing the prosecutor, Emrys omits his father's role, then watches his father turn himself in anyway, refusing to be his son's omission. POV: Emrys. Beat: grief and grudging respect.

chapters.title: What We Carry Forward
chapters.summary: Months later, Lena resumes her archive work with Emrys's help; Saint Alder's becomes a memorial. Emrys donates the diary, keeping only its first page — and finally sleeps without remembering everything. POV: Emrys. Beat: inheritance chosen, not imposed.
